answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring every participant to post a bond before it may route payments or vote. Think of that bond as an anchor: spinning up a fresh jetty is free for an attacker, but each new jetty must carry its own identical anchor. To flood the ocean with fake peers, the adversary must burn one full bond per Sybil, so the price of influence grows linearly with the number of identities, and any detected double-vote forfeits it.
